newsitem.title: JAPAN: Keihin Seiki to merge with two car parts makers.
newsitem.headline: Keihin Seiki to merge with two car parts makers.

text.p: Keihin Seiki Manufacturing Co Ltd, a manufacturer of carburettors and other car parts, said on Wednesday that it would merge with two other car component makers from next April.

Keihin Seiki said the two other companies, Honda Air and Device System and Denshi Giken Co Ltd, would be dissolved in the merger, which was aimed at boosting efficiency, competitiveness and investment.
The merged firm will be called Keihin Corp.
Honda Motor Co Ltd is the largest shareholder of all three firms, Keihin Seiki said.
Keihin Seiki said it would issue 28.44 million new shares for the merger.
Each Honda Air share would be exchanged for 3.9 new Keihin shares and each Denshi Giken share for 13.5 of the new shares, Keihin Seiki said.
Keihin Seiki forecast that Keihin Corp would a post parent current profit of 5.4 billion yen in the year to March 31, 1998, rising to 5.6 billion yen in fiscal 1998/99.
It forecast an annual dividend for the merged firm of 10 yen for both business years.
In 1995/96, Keihin Seiki posted a parent current profit of 1.83 billion yen and paid an annual dividend of 8.5 yen.
Honda Air posted a parent current profit of 1.61 billion yen in 1995/96 and paid an annual dividend of 50 yen.
Denshi Giken posted a parent current profit of 1.86 billion yen in 1995/96 and paid an annual dividend of 125 yen.
As of the end of March 1996, Keihin Seiki was 34.6 percent owned by Honda Motor. The car maker owned 43.0 percent of Honda Air and 65.5 percent by Denshi as of that date.
